title: Make scaffold substitution cover Rust imports and application identity
description: Observed in newly generated xlatch: crates renamed to xlatch-* but use rust_core remains in CLI/API/MCP and generate_config. APP_NAME, schema tests/URLs, repository metadata and config paths still say rust-workspace. This prevents compilation and risks config-directory collisions. Add a rendered non-default-name smoke fixture that compiles generated targets/examples and asserts project identity is substituted consistently.

title: Ship secure API defaults without unauthenticated config disclosure
description: rust-workspace API exposes GET /config returning the complete AppConfig and configures CORS origin/method/header Any. Future config fields may include secrets. Remove config disclosure from the base scaffold or implement explicit authenticated, redacted admin access. Omit CORS by default; opt into exact required origins. Add a regression asserting the default API cannot expose configuration/secrets.

title: Add pull-request CI that validates rendered templates before release
description: xlatch scaffold has only .github/workflows/release.yml, no pull-request CI. Add template-render tests for representative names including hyphens, compile/test examples and binary entrypoints, rustfmt/Clippy on touched scope, and dependency/security checks. Use minimal workflow token permissions, pinned third-party actions and a concurrency policy; separate release credentials from PR builds. Gate releases on successful validation. Keep checks proportional and deterministic.

title: Streamline generated AGENTS.md into accurate enforceable guardrails
description: Generated AGENTS.md is ~300 lines and repeats code/file maps and generic CLI conventions. It specifies rmcp 1.2 although Cargo.toml uses 2.2, .beads/issues.jsonl although trx stores .trx, and contradicts narrow-test guidance with broader config/commit commands. Replace copied inventories with a short canonical workflow and references to machine-checked config. Retain explicit boundaries: preserve unrelated work, no secret logs/unauthenticated config endpoints, approval bound to real reviewed scope, honest validation evidence, no placeholder behavior presented as complete. Add drift checks for named commands and crate/version references; avoid blanket doc/flag boilerplate that generates slop.

title: Restrict template application formats to JSON and TOML
description: User requires JSON/TOML only. Remove YAML CLI examples/output and serde_yaml dependencies from generated applications; disable config default features and enable only json/toml. Update AGENTS guidance so agents do not introduce YAML application formats.

title: Require real privilege-boundary tests and anchored secret migration in service templates
description: Lessons from xlatch protected mode: a separate service account is insufficient if agent-authored commands inherit that identity, if source TLS keys remain user-readable, or if user-writable trust roots are copied without an independently verified anchor. Add concise template guardrails requiring separate executors, ownership and ACL checks including ancestor directories, explicit file modes independent of umask, credential rotation during privilege migration, and negative cross-user integration tests. Distinguish unit/API checks from actual OS enforcement and never report protected installation complete before the privileged setup and runtime checks pass. Keep AGENTS.md concise and put reusable acceptance harnesses in scripts; avoid generic checklist prose.
